1.title: HTML is Markup, Not Programming
1.theory:
## What HTML is HTML — **HyperText Markup Language**. It is **markup**, not programming. HTML describes the **structure** of a document: "this is a heading", "this is a paragraph", "this is a link". There are no variables, loops, or conditions. A browser reads the HTML and **renders** it: headings become large bold text, links become clickable, images appear on the page. ## What HTML is not - Not a programming language (no logic). - Not styling — that is CSS. - Not interactivity — that is JavaScript. If you know Python or Java: HTML has no `if`, no `for`, no functions. It is closer to a Markdown document than to code. ## Tags A document is made of **tags**: ```html

Hello

This is a paragraph.

``` The opening and closing tags (with `/`) wrap the content. Together with the content they form an **element**. - `

` — opening tag - `Hello` — content - `

` — closing tag - Whole thing — element ## Self-closing tags Some have no content: ```html
``` `
` — line break. `` — image. `
` and `` are not needed. ## Attributes In the opening tag you can add **attributes** — `name="value"` pairs: ```html Example ``` `href` — where the link goes. `src` — image URL. `alt` — text alternative. ## What the browser sees The browser parses tags, builds a **DOM** and paints it. The user sees the result — tags are not visible on screen. ## What if - Forget to close a tag — the browser often closes it for you, but the structure can be wrong. - Nest tags incorrectly — `

` — the browser may rearrange the DOM. - Use `<` in text — must escape as `<`, otherwise the parser treats it as a tag. ## Common mistake Text **outside** any tag: `Hello

world

` — the browser shows "Hello" but it lives in `` without structure. Wrap visible content in a tag. ## Summary - HTML is markup, not programming - Elements: `content` - Self-closing: `
`, `` - Attributes: `name="value"` in the opening tag - Text must live inside tags

options: A markup language for document structure

2.title: First Document
2.theory:
## Skeleton of every HTML page ```html My Page

Hello

``` Every line has a purpose. ## First line. Tells the browser: "this is modern HTML5". Without it the browser uses **quirks mode** and renders differently. Always put it first. ## The root element. Everything lives inside it. `lang="en"` — document language (helps screen readers and translation). ## — invisible Content of `` is **not shown** to the user. It holds metadata: encoding (``), title (``), linked styles. `<title>` shows in the **browser tab**. ## <body> — visible Everything the user sees goes in `<body>`: headings, paragraphs, images, forms. ## Why structure matters The browser builds the DOM from the structure. Without `<html>`/`<head>`/`<body>` it still renders — but invalid, and tools (search engines, screen readers) get confused. ## What if - Forget `<!DOCTYPE html>` — quirks mode, unpredictable rendering. - Put visible content in `<head>` — moved to `<body>` or hidden. - Forget `<title>` — the tab shows the file name. - No `charset` — non-ASCII text becomes mojibake. ## Common mistake Writing everything in `<body>` without `<head>`. Works visually, but without `<meta charset>` non-ASCII text breaks. ## Summary - `<!DOCTYPE html>` — first line - `<html lang="...">` — root - `<head>` — invisible: `title`, `meta`, styles - `<body>` — visible content - `charset="UTF-8"` — for Unicode

4.title: Comments
4.theory:
## Why Code lives longer than memory. Comments explain **why** and **what** to yourself in six months and to others today. In HTML they also **temporarily disable** a block. ## Syntax ```html

Visible text

``` Starts with ``. Everything between is **ignored** by the browser. ## Visible in source Open dev tools (F12) — comments are there. Never put passwords, API keys, personal data. Real secrets do not live in HTML. ## Temporarily disabling ```html

Shown

``` The first `

` is inside a comment — the browser treats it as text. ## Nested comments do not work ```html outer --> ``` The first `-->` closes the comment. The parser sees `outer -->` as broken markup. Do not nest. ## What if - `` — everything up to EOF becomes a comment. - `--` inside (``) — technically invalid. - Comment out a block and forget to re-enable — page looks broken. ## Common mistake Forget `-->`. Everything after `` or EOF. Page is blank. ## Summary - `` — comment - Browser ignores - Visible in dev tools — no secrets - Nested comments break - Forgot `-->` — hid the rest of the page

6.title: Links: a href
6.theory:
## The anchor tag ```html Click ``` - `` — anchor, link. - `href` — destination URL. - Text between tags — what is clickable. ## Absolute vs relative **Absolute** — full URL: `https://example.com/page`. **Relative** — path from the current page: `page.html`, `/about`, `../docs/file.html`. Absolute — for external sites. Relative — inside your site. ## target ```html New tab ``` `target="_blank"` — opens in a new tab. Without it — in the same tab. ## Anchors inside a page ```html To section 2

Section 2

``` Click scrolls to the element with that `id`. `#top` without an element — scroll to top. ## mailto and tel ```html Write Call ``` Open mail client or phone (on mobile). ## Nested tags Wrap an image: ```html ``` Click on the image — navigation. ## Link text Bad: `click here`. Good: `Download price list`. Screen readers read only the link text. ## What if - No `href` — `` without URL, not clickable. - `href=""` — reloads the page. - `href="javascript:..."` — legacy anti-pattern. ## Common mistake `` without `https://` for external — the browser treats it as a relative path to your domain. ## Summary - `text` — link - Absolute — full URL, relative — path - `target="_blank"` — new tab - `#id` — anchor inside page - `mailto:` / `tel:` - Link text — meaningful

7.title: Images: img src alt
7.theory: ## The img tag ```html ``` - `src` — path to the image (URL or relative). - `alt` — text if the image fails or for a screen reader. `` — **self-closing**. `` is not needed. ## Why alt - **Screen reader** reads `alt` aloud. Without `alt` the user has no idea what is on the image. - **Image did not load** — `alt` is shown instead. - **SEO** — search engines read `alt`. `alt=""` (empty) — if the image is **decorative**, no meaning. ## Sizes ```html ``` `width` / `height` — in pixels. Optional, but useful: the browser reserves space and does not "jump" while loading. ## Formats - `.jpg` / `.jpeg` — photos. - `.png` — transparency. - `.svg` — vector (logos, icons). - `.webp` — modern, smaller. ## Image as a link ```html ``` Click on the image — navigation. ## What if - Forget `src` — empty image or broken icon. - No `alt` — screen reader reads the file name (`cat.jpg`). - Wrong `src` — broken icon + `alt`. - Forget to close — fine, `` is void. ## Common mistake `alt="image"` or `alt="img"` — useless. `alt` must describe what is in the image: `alt="A cat sleeping on a windowsill"`. ## Summary - `` - `alt` is required (empty if decorative) - `width` / `height` — reserve space - Image can live inside `` - Self-closing

13.title: form, input, label
13.theory:
## Why forms

A form collects data from the user: login, search, checkout. Data goes to the server.

## form

```html
<form>
  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input type="text" id="name" name="name">
</form>
```

`<form>` — container. `action` — where to send, `method` — GET/POST (later).

## input

`<input>` — self-closing. Type via `type`:

```html
<input type="text">
<input type="email">
<input type="password">
```

`name` — field name for submission. `id` — for linking with `<label>`.

## label

Label for a field. Linked via `for` (on label) = `id` (on input):

```html
<label for="age">Age</label>
<input type="number" id="age" name="age">
```

Click on the label — focus on the field. Screen reader reads the `label` aloud.

## Without for/id

You can nest input inside label:

```html
<label>Name <input type="text"></label>
```

Also works: click on label focuses the input. Both variants are valid.

## Why for/id is better

Explicit link works even if the label is far from the input. And styling is easier.

## What if

- No `for`/`id` — click on the label does not focus the field.
- Duplicate `id` — invalid, `for` binds to the first one.
- `label` without `input` — meaningless (just text).

## Common mistake

`<label>Name</label><input>` — the label is nearby but not linked. Click does not work, the screen reader does not associate them.

## Summary

- `<form>` — container
- `<input type="...">` — field
- `<label for="id">` = `<input id="id">` — link
- Click on label → focus on input
- Screen reader reads the label

14.title: Input Types
14.theory:
## Why different types

`<input type="text">` — universal. But **type hints** the browser what to enter: on mobile, email — keyboard with `@`, number — numeric keyboard.

## text

```html
<input type="text">
```

Plain text.

## email

```html
<input type="email">
```

On submit the browser checks the format (`@` and a dot).

## password

```html
<input type="password">
```

Characters hidden with dots. In HTML the value is still plaintext — HTTPS is required.

## number

```html
<input type="number" min="1" max="100">
```

Numbers only. `min`/`max` — range.

## checkbox

```html
<label><input type="checkbox"> I agree</label>
```

Multiple choices, any number.

## radio

```html
<label><input type="radio" name="color" value="red"> Red</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="color" value="blue"> Blue</label>
```

One option per group. **Same `name`** for the group.

## Others

- `type="tel"` — phone, mobile keyboard.
- `type="date"` — date, calendar.
- `type="url"` — URL.
- `type="file"` — file upload.

## What if

- `radio` with different `name` — you can select all, not one group.
- `checkbox` with same `name` — browser submits an array, better avoid.
- `type="number"` with letters — browser blocks (on desktop).

## Common mistake

`radio` for a single switch — meaning lost. `radio` — for two or more options. For one — `checkbox`.

## Summary

- `text`, `email`, `password`, `number` — main types
- `checkbox` — multiple, `radio` — one from group
- `radio` share the same `name`
- `min`/`max` for number
- Type helps the browser and mobile keyboard

15.title: textarea, select, option, button
15.theory:
## textarea

Multi-line field:

```html
<textarea rows="4" cols="40"></textarea>
```

**Not** self-closing! Needs a closing `</textarea>`. `rows` — visible lines, `cols` — width.

## select and option

Dropdown:

```html
<select name="city">
  <option value="msk">Moscow</option>
  <option value="spb">SPb</option>
</select>
```

`<option>` — a choice. `value` — what is sent to the server, text — what the user sees.

## Option groups

```html
<select>
  <optgroup label="Europe">
    <option>Moscow</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>
```

`<optgroup>` — grouping.

## button

```html
<button type="submit">Send</button>
<button type="button">Button</button>
```

- `type="submit"` — submit the form (default).
- `type="button"` — just a button (for JS).
- `type="reset"` — reset the form.

`<button>` — with text inside, unlike `<input type="submit">`.

## Multiple lines in textarea

```html
<textarea>Line 1
Line 2</textarea>
```

Everything inside `<textarea>` is the default value (do not wrap in tags!).

## What if

- `<textarea/>` self-closing — breaks all the HTML that follows.
- `<select>` without `<option>` — empty list.
- `<button>` without `type` inside `<form>` — defaults to submit, may accidentally send.

## Common mistake

`<textarea value="text">` — does not work, value is set by the content between tags. `<input value>` — yes, but not `<textarea>`.

## Summary

- `<textarea></textarea>` — multi-line
- `<select>` + `<option>` — dropdown
- `<button type="submit">` — send
- `<button type="button">` — plain
- Inside textarea — only text

16.title: HTML Validation
16.theory:
## Why validation

The user can make mistakes: empty field, wrong email. **HTML validation** — a check before submission. Without JavaScript, on the browser side.

## required

```html
<input type="text" required>
```

Mandatory field. Empty — the form does not submit, the browser highlights it.

## type="email"

Already validation: needs `@` and something after.

## pattern

A regular expression:

```html
<input type="text" pattern="[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{3}">
```

Format "123-456". Does not match — does not submit.

## minlength / maxlength

```html
<input type="text" minlength="3" maxlength="10">
```

Minimum/maximum characters.

## min / max / step for number

```html
<input type="number" min="1" max="100" step="1">
```

Range and step.

## Error message

The browser shows its own. Custom — via `setCustomValidity` (JS, later).

## What if

- `required` on a hidden field — form does not submit, unclear why.
- Invalid `pattern` (bad regex) — the browser ignores it.
- Client-only validation — the server must validate anyway.

## Common mistake

Relying only on HTML validation. It is easy to bypass (disable JS, send a raw request). The server also validates.

## Summary

- `required` — mandatory
- `type="email"` — email format
- `pattern` — regex
- `minlength` / `maxlength`
- `min` / `max` / `step` for number
- The server validates anyway

questions.text: Can you rely only on HTML validation?
options: No, the server must validate too

19.title: video, audio, iframe
19.theory:
## video

```html
<video src="movie.mp4" controls></video>
```

- `controls` — control panel (play/pause/volume).
- `src` — file path.

## source

Several formats — the browser picks a supported one:

```html
<video controls>
  <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="movie.webm" type="video/webm">
</video>
```

## video attributes

- `autoplay` — play immediately (often blocked without `muted`).
- `muted` — no sound.
- `loop` — loop.
- `poster` — image before playback.

## audio

```html
<audio controls src="sound.mp3"></audio>
```

Same, but sound only. Smaller panel.

## iframe

Embeds **another page**:

```html
<iframe src="https://example.com" width="600" height="400"></iframe>
```

Often for YouTube, maps, widgets.

## iframe security

- `sandbox` — restricts what can happen inside.
- Embedding other sites may violate their `X-Frame-Options`.
- Your own content — fine.

## What if

- Forget `controls` — video with no buttons, autoplay only if `autoplay`.
- `autoplay` without `muted` — most browsers block.
- `<iframe>` to a site that forbids embedding — empty white block.

## Common mistake

`<video autoplay src="...">` without `muted` — does not play. Browsers block autoplay with sound.

## Summary

- `<video controls>` — video with controls
- `<source>` — multiple formats
- `<audio controls>` — sound
- `<iframe src="...">` — embedded page
- `autoplay` usually requires `muted`

24.title: meta: charset, viewport, description
24.theory:
## meta in head

Page metadata: encoding, scaling, description. **Not visible** to the user, but important for the browser and search engines.

## charset

```html
<meta charset="UTF-8">
```

Text encoding. Without it non-ASCII characters break. **Always first** in `<head>`.

## viewport

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
```

Mobile adaptation. Without it on a phone the page renders as on a big screen — tiny, with horizontal scroll.

## description

```html
<meta name="description" content="HTML course">
```

A short page description. May appear in search results. Affects SEO.

## Other common ones

```html
<meta name="author" content="Ivan">
<meta property="og:title" content="Title">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#ffffff">
```

`og:*` — for social networks (Open Graph): how the preview looks when shared.

## What if

- No `charset` — mojibake (ÐŸÑ€Ð¸Ð²ÐµÑ‚).
- No `viewport` — tiny text on mobile.
- `description` longer than 160 chars — truncated in search results.

## Common mistake

`charset` not at the start of `<head>` — the browser may already start parsing with the wrong encoding. Put it first.

## Summary

- `charset` — mandatory, first
- `viewport` — for mobile
- `description` — for search engines
- `og:*` — for social networks
- Not visible on the page, but critical

28.title: fieldset, legend
28.theory:
## Why group fields

A 10-field form without grouping is a wall. Logical blocks ("Personal", "Address", "Payment") help the user and the screen reader.

## fieldset

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Personal</legend>
  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input type="text" id="name">
</fieldset>
```

`<fieldset>` — a box around a group. Semantic: "these fields belong together".

## legend

`<legend>` — title of the group. **First** child of `<fieldset>`. The browser renders it in the frame.

Without `<legend>` — a box with no label, the screen reader can't tell what the group is.

## disabled on fieldset

```html
<fieldset disabled>
  <input type="text">
  <button>OK</button>
</fieldset>
```

All fields inside — disabled and not submitted. Handy for "pause the whole block".

## Nested

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Address</legend>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>City</legend>
    <input type="text">
  </fieldset>
</fieldset>
```

Nesting allowed. Don't overdo it — 2 levels is enough.

## Accessibility

The screen reader reads `legend` as the group header and when jumping to each field announces: "Personal, Name, text field". Without `fieldset` — just "Name, text field".

## What if

- `<legend>` not first — the browser may render it, but semantics break.
- `<fieldset>` without `legend` — meaning lost.
- `<legend>` outside `<fieldset>` — invalid.

## Common mistake

Replacing `<fieldset>` with a `<div>` with a class. Visually similar, but semantics lost and `disabled` on the group doesn't work.

## Summary

- `<fieldset>` — group of fields
- `<legend>` — title, first child
- `disabled` on `<fieldset>` — whole group
- Helps the screen reader
- Don't replace with `<div>`

questions.explanation: Group of fields with shared semantics.

29.title: datalist
29.theory:
## What datalist is

`<datalist>` — list of **suggestions** for `<input>`. The user can pick from the list or type their own. Doesn't block input.

## Syntax

```html
<input list="cities" name="city">
<datalist id="cities">
  <option value="Moscow">
  <option value="Saint Petersburg">
  <option value="Kazan">
</datalist>
```

- `<input list="id">` — link to datalist by `id`.
- `<datalist id="...">` — the list.
- `<option value="...">` — variants.

## Not the same as select

`<select>` — only from the list, input locked. `<datalist>` — suggestions, free entry.

```html
<!-- select: only from list -->
<select><option>Moscow</option></select>

<!-- datalist: suggestions + free entry -->
<input list="x">
<datalist id="x"><option value="Moscow"></datalist>
```

## option value

In `<datalist>` only `value` works. Text inside `<option>` is often ignored — put content in `value`.

## When to use

- Autocomplete cities, countries.
- Frequent values (email domains).
- Search with suggestions.

## What if

- `list="x"` without `<datalist id="x">` — no suggestions, but typing works.
- `<datalist>` without `id` — won't link.
- `<option>` without `value` — variant won't work.

## Common mistake

`<datalist>` with text in `<option>` and no `value` — the browser won't show the suggestion. Always `value="..."`.

## Summary

- `<input list="id">` + `<datalist id="...">`
- Suggestions, doesn't block input
- `<option value="...">` — variants
- Not a `<select>` replacement
- Always `value`

Can you type your own value?

30.title: More input types
30.theory:
## date, time, datetime-local

```html
<input type="date">
<input type="time">
<input type="datetime-local">
```

Open the built-in calendar / time picker. Value comes as `2024-01-15` / `14:30`.

## color

```html
<input type="color" value="#ff0000">
```

Color palette. Returns `#rrggbb`.

## range

```html
<input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" step="5">
```

Slider. `min` / `max` / `step`. Ideal for volume, brightness.

## file

```html
<input type="file" accept="image/*" multiple>
```

- `accept` — allowed types (`.jpg,.png`, `image/*`, `application/pdf`).
- `multiple` — several files.

**Not sent** without `enctype="multipart/form-data"` on `<form>`.

## search

```html
<input type="search">
```

Like `text`, but with a clear button. Semantics: search.

## tel, url

```html
<input type="tel">
<input type="url">
```

`tel` — mobile keyboard with digits. `url` — URL format check.

## What if

- `type="date"` in a browser without calendar (old) — renders as text.
- `<form>` without `enctype` with `type="file"` — file not sent.
- `range` without `step` — step 1 by default.

## Common mistake

`type="file"` without `enctype="multipart/form-data"` — file not sent. Common issue.

## Summary

- `date`, `time`, `datetime-local` — date/time
- `color` — palette
- `range` — slider
- `file` — upload (+ `enctype` on form)
- `search`, `tel`, `url` — mobile keyboard and validation

31.title: output, progress, meter
31.theory:
## output

Field for a **result** of calculation. Linked to inputs via `for`:

```html
<input type="number" id="a" value="5">
+ <input type="number" id="b" value="3">
= <output for="a b">8</output>
```

Static by itself — value changes via JS. Semantics: "this is a result".

## progress

**Task completion indicator** (download, progress):

```html
<progress value="30" max="100">30%</progress>
```

- `value` — done so far.
- `max` — total.
- Text inside — fallback for old browsers.
- No `value` — indeterminate (spinner without %).

## meter

**Measurement in a known range** (battery, temperature, grade):

```html
<meter value="0.7" min="0" max="1">70%</meter>
```

- `value` — current.
- `min` / `max` — range.
- `low` / `high` / `optimum` — colors (green / yellow / red by value).

## progress vs meter

- `<progress>` — "how much of the task is done" (0 → max, one direction).
- `<meter>` — "where we are in the range" (can be bad or good).

Battery 70% — `meter` (bad if 10%). Download 70% — `progress` (just not finished).

## What if

- `<progress>` without `max` — default 1.
- `<meter>` with `value` outside `min`/`max` — browser clips.
- `<output>` without JS — static text.

## Common mistake

Confusing `<progress>` and `<meter>`. If the scale is "bad-good" — meter. If "done-not done" — progress.

## Summary

- `<output>` — result
- `<progress>` — task (value / max)
- `<meter>` — measurement (min / max / low / high)
- Download — progress, battery — meter

32.title: srcset, sizes: responsive images
32.theory: ## The problem A 2000×1500 image on a phone with a 400px screen — 500 KB downloaded for nothing. Need **different versions** for different screens. ## srcset ```html ``` - `src` — fallback for old browsers. - `srcset` — variants with `w` descriptor (width in pixels). - Browser picks based on screen width and DPR. ## x descriptor ```html ``` `x` — pixel density (for Retina). `2x` — double. ## sizes Tells the browser **how much space** the image takes: ```html ``` - `(max-width: 600px) 100vw` — on narrow, image takes 100% of window. - `50vw` — on wide, 50%. Without `sizes` the browser assumes 100vw. ## Tips - `srcset` with `w` + `sizes` — responsive. - `srcset` with `x` — retina (logos). - Don't duplicate `src` and first `srcset` — redundant. ## What if - `srcset` without `sizes` and `w` — browser takes first. - Typo in filename — broken image. - `sizes` with wrong media conditions — wrong size. ## Common mistake Forget `sizes` with `w`. Without it the browser thinks the image is always 100vw and picks the smallest. ## Summary - `srcset` — variants - `w` — width, `x` — density - `sizes` — how much space - Browser chooses - `src` — fallback

37.title: canvas
37.theory:
## What it is

`<canvas>` — area for drawing via JS. Pixel canvas for shapes, charts, games.

## Syntax

```html
<canvas id="c" width="200" height="100"></canvas>
```

Without JS — empty rectangle.

## Context

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById("c");
const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
ctx.fillStyle = "red";
ctx.fillRect(10, 10, 50, 30);
```

- `getContext("2d")` — 2D drawing.
- `getContext("webgl")` — 3D (WebGL).
- `fillStyle` / `fillRect` — fill and rectangle.

## Basic methods

- `fillRect(x, y, w, h)` — fill rectangle.
- `strokeRect` — outline.
- `beginPath` / `moveTo` / `lineTo` / `stroke` — lines.
- `arc(x, y, r, 0, 2π)` — circle.
- `fillText("hi", x, y)` — text.

## Canvas vs SVG

- **Canvas** — pixels, faster for animations, no DOM (not stylable via CSS, elements not findable).
- **SVG** — vector, each element in DOM, stylable and manageable.

For games — canvas. For icons and charts — SVG.

## Size vs CSS

`width` / `height` on element — **real canvas pixels**. CSS `width` — display. Mismatch — blur.

```html
<canvas width="400" height="300" style="width: 200px"></canvas>
```

Canvas 400×300 displayed as 200 — 2x DPR, sharp on retina.

## What if

- No `getContext` — nothing drawn.
- `width` / `height` not set — 300×150 default.
- Draw before canvas loaded — `null`.

## Common mistake

CSS `width` confused with attribute `width`. CSS stretches/shrinks, but real size from attribute.

## Summary

- `<canvas>` — drawing canvas
- `getContext("2d")` — context
- JS draws
- CSS width ≠ real size
- vs SVG: pixels vs vector

39.title: Practice: registration form
39.theory:
## Task

Registration form with all studied elements: `fieldset`, `label`, `required`, `pattern`, different input types, `datalist`.

## Contents

- `<form>` with `method="post"`.
- `<fieldset>` "Personal" — name (`text`, `required`), email (`email`, `required`).
- `<fieldset>` "Account" — password (`password`, `required`, `minlength="6"`), date of birth (`date`).
- `<fieldset>` "Settings" — country from `datalist`, consent (`checkbox`, `required`).
- `<button type="submit">` — submit.

## Checks

- All fields with `label for` = `id`.
- `required` on mandatory.
- `minlength="6"` on password.
- `datalist` for country.
- `submit` button.

## Structure

```html
<form method="post">
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Personal</legend>
    <label for="name">Name</label>
    <input type="text" id="name" required>
  </fieldset>
  <!-- ... -->
</form>
```

## What if

- No `required` — form submits with empty fields.
- `<fieldset>` without `<legend>` — semantics lost.
- `label` without `for` — click doesn't focus.

## Common mistake

All fields in one pile without `fieldset`. Works, but hard to fill and hard for screen readers.

## Summary

- `fieldset` + `legend` for grouping
- `label for` = `input id`
- `required`, `minlength`
- `datalist` for suggestions
- `type="submit"`
